name: Options Pairs / Relative-Value Trade
aliases: long A calls vs long B puts
summary: Express a relative view between two related underlyings with options rather than shares - long calls (or a call spread) on the favored name against long puts (or a put spread) on the disfavored one - so the pair has convexity and a capped loss instead of two open equity legs.

legs.strike_rule: underlying A (the favored name): call delta 0.35-0.45, or a call debit spread with the short at 0.15-0.20 delta to cut cost
underlying B (the disfavored name): |put delta| 0.35-0.45, or a put debit spread; contract count beta- and notional-adjusted so both legs carry equal dollar delta

max_profit: Large and asymmetric: both legs can pay if A rises and B falls; capped only if debit spreads are used, unbounded on the call side if outright
max_loss: The total debit paid - which is the whole reason to use options rather than a long/short share pair
breakevens: Each leg has its own; the pair breaks even when the summed intrinsic values at expiry equal the total debit

greeks.delta: positive on A, negative on B, dollar-matched to roughly zero net market delta
greeks.theta: negative on both legs - the pair pays rent every day
greeks.vega: positive on both legs, so the pair is implicitly long vol

when_to_use: A spread view with a catalyst and a deadline - one name reporting into a sector others have already guided down, an index-inclusion candidate versus its sector, a merger's acquirer versus a clean comparable. Prefer this over a share pair when the account cannot or should not carry a short stock leg, which on this account is always.
entry_rules: Both underlyings must be genuinely related: same sector or an established correlation >= 0.6 over 120 days. A pair without a linkage is two unrelated bets.
Dollar-delta match at entry within 10%: contracts_A x delta_A x spot_A approximately equals contracts_B x |delta_B| x spot_B.
Total debit <= 1.5% of equity per pair; at most 3 pairs open at once.
Use debit spreads rather than outrights whenever the outright package costs more than 1.5% of equity - the short leg of each spread is covered by the long, keeping the structure at level 3.
Both legs same expiry; expiry must be at least 14 days beyond the catalyst date.
OI >= 250 on every leg; no leg whose bid/ask exceeds 10% of its mid.
Never build the B leg as a short call - the bearish leg is always a long put or a put debit spread on this account.
management_rules: Take profit at 60% of the maximum modeled pair value, or when the spread between A and B reaches the target ratio, whichever comes first.
Close both legs together. A pair that has become a single outright position is no longer the trade that was entered - if one leg is closed, close the other within the session.
Re-match dollar delta if the ratio drifts more than 25% from entry, by adjusting contracts on the cheaper side only.
Time stop: close at 21 DTE regardless of P/L; the theta on two long legs compounds.
Cut the pair immediately if the correlation that justified it breaks (120-day correlation falls below 0.4).
exit_rules: Close all legs at least 2 trading days before expiration; never allow auto-exercise on either side.
If debit spreads are used, close each short leg at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85, and short calls before any ex-dividend date while ITM.
Close, do not exercise, any ITM long leg.
Log the pair as one position throughout; partial closes must be recorded as a structure change, not a new trade.
assignment_risk: None in the outright version (all legs long). In the debit-spread version each short leg is covered by a long of the same right and expiry, so assignment is defined but still delivers shares in two different underlyings - the pre-expiry close rule is what keeps the account clean.
buying_power: The net debit only; spread versions hold nothing beyond their debit because every short is long-covered.
liquidity_needs: Both chains must be liquid at the same expiry - the binding constraint is usually the smaller of the two names.
common_mistakes: Matching contract counts instead of dollar delta; letting the winning leg run while the losing leg expires, which converts a pair into an outright; building the bearish leg as a short call and discovering it is naked.
zero_dte_notes: Not appropriate - a relative-value view needs weeks, and two 0DTE long legs is just paying double theta.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
